ablations.expected_regression: resume correctness should fall because scene integrity is no longer checked.
unsupported and invalid memory use should increase.
claim support and evidence citation quality should degrade.
fault localization should revert toward raw-log inspection.
policy and artifact lineage drift should slip through resume.
evidence-retaining replay should lose sensitivity to evidence drift.
authorization and commit-time evidence should become weaker.

caveats: not a governed claim commit protocol
baselines.name: LangGraph-style durable execution

caveats: session persistence is not proof of scene integrity
baselines.name: OpenHands-style coding agent

data_availability_statement: A replication package should include anonymized task specs, fault injection scripts, baseline adapters, ablation toggles, provenance/oracle audit receipts, and evaluation notebooks.

fault_scenarios.description: Pause execution between major steps and require hydration before resumption.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: resume from a retained scene manifest instead of a raw transcript.
fault_scenarios.title: Mid-run interruption

fault_scenarios.description: Remove policy or artifact lineage from a compressed state summary.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: pin policy and artifact lineage in the checkpoint summary.
fault_scenarios.title: Compaction drift

fault_scenarios.description: Offload or edit active context while losing a required policy, evidence, or artifact pin needed for safe hydration.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: treat context editing as a governed action that must retain pinned claims and active execution frame refs.
fault_scenarios.title: Context manager dropped pin

fault_scenarios.description: Return an outdated or contradicted tool result and measure recovery.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: compare cached prefix and live suffix against the baseline trace.
fault_scenarios.title: Stale tool output

fault_scenarios.description: Delete a required artifact reference before phase exit or report write-up.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: refuse phase exit until required artifacts are restored.
fault_scenarios.title: Missing artifact

fault_scenarios.description: Change or contaminate the task oracle, gold patch, test patch, or executable environment metadata used to score an issue-to-patch task.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: record task provenance, test oracle fingerprints, environment metadata, and contamination/audit receipts in the artifact package.
fault_scenarios.title: Benchmark oracle drift

fault_scenarios.description: Attempt to cite quarantined or inactive evidence in a claim or report.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: require an active evidence claim before commit.
fault_scenarios.title: Quarantined evidence citation

fault_scenarios.description: Let authority evidence expire before a privileged effect commit.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: reattach a fresh witness before commit.
fault_scenarios.title: Expired approval

fault_scenarios.description: Commit a belief that is unsupported by the active evidence ledger.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: stage, validate, and only then commit memory.
fault_scenarios.title: Wrong memory commit

fault_scenarios.description: Reuse a stale or similar-task belief that conflicts with the current evidence scene.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: block decision projection until stale or conflicting memory is revalidated against active evidence.
fault_scenarios.title: Memory interference

fault_scenarios.description: Change the evidence intake component, such as lexical versus dense retrieval, and observe claim support drift.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: record retrieval component fingerprints and require active evidence claims before memory/writeup commit.
fault_scenarios.title: Retrieval component shift

fault_scenarios.description: Keep the evidence payload plausible while corrupting freshness, lineage, source, or metadata predicates.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: gate memory/writeup commit on data-quality predicates, freshness receipts, and lineage checks.
fault_scenarios.title: Silent evidence defect

fault_scenarios.description: Change official SWE-bench results, per-instance receipts, run logs, or oracle fingerprints after Docker execution.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: retain official results.json, instance_results.jsonl, run logs, execution receipts, and hydration reports together.
fault_scenarios.title: Official execution receipt drift

fault_scenarios.description: Swap model/provider capability snapshots mid-run and check if trace contracts still match.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: checkpoint provider capability snapshots together with the scene.
fault_scenarios.title: Provider switch drift

fault_scenarios.description: Change the tool contract hash or normalization rules between runs.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: persist tool contract fingerprints alongside traces.
fault_scenarios.title: Tool schema drift

fault_scenarios.description: Keep the action the same but change the evidence ledger fingerprint or claim ids.
fault_scenarios.mitigation_hint: treat the evidence scene as part of the replay contract.
fault_scenarios.title: Evidence receipt drift

research_questions.question: Does scene-based hydration improve correct task resumption compared with transcript-based or checkpoint-only baselines?
Does governed memory commit reduce invalid, stale, and interference-induced memory use and unsupported claims in long-horizon agent tasks?
Can trace-envelope-driven transition graphs localize and reproduce long-horizon agent failures more accurately than raw logs?
What is the overhead of scene-based governance, and can it remain practical for software-engineering agents?
